# Kernel options the dcfs QEMU tests need (step 3.1a, kept by step 24.2).
#
# The test kernel is Alpine's linux-virt, so this is no longer a build
# fragment: it is the list of what the tests rely on, each with a comment
# saying who needs it, and //third_party/linux:kernel_config_test checks it
# against the package's /boot/config-*. An option listed `=y` must be built in
# or a module (=m) there, never off; a module also has to be in the `modules`
# of the tests that use it (test/qemu/qemu_test.bzl). An option listed
# `=builtin` must be built in: nothing can load a module before it is needed
# (the console, the virtio-mmio devices, which the kernel learns of from its
# command line, something insmod does not read; the initramfs; the mounts
# guest/init does first; module loading itself). Add a line
# here, with the reason, when a test starts to need another option, so later
# phases never have to edit anything else (docs/plan/execution.md, "Kernel
# config once").
#
# Left out on purpose: CONFIG_DM_DUST (Alpine does not build it; Phase 11
# injects errors with dm-error and dm-flakey, which it does).

# --- foundational symbols tinyconfig's allnoconfig-style baseline turns off
# that a normal defconfig gets "for free" (every one of these is a
# `menuconfig`/`bool ... if EXPERT`-style symbol with a `default y` that
# allnoconfig/tinyconfig ignores -- it must be requested explicitly here, or
# everything nested under it silently disappears instead of failing loudly;
# see README.md's "Kconfig dependency notes").
# Block layer: wraps every block device driver and block-based filesystem
# (virtio-blk, ext4, xfs, btrfs, device-mapper, loop) below.
CONFIG_BLOCK=y
# Virtio bus support menu: wraps every CONFIG_VIRTIO_* driver below.
CONFIG_VIRTIO_MENU=y
# Guest/host hypervisor-detection menu: wraps PARAVIRT/KVM_GUEST/PVH below.
CONFIG_HYPERVISOR_GUEST=y
# TTY layer: wraps the serial console drivers below; also depended on
# directly by CONFIG_VIRTIO_CONSOLE.
CONFIG_TTY=y
# Non-root users/groups/capabilities: depended on directly by
# CONFIG_NAMESPACES and CONFIG_NFS_FS below.
CONFIG_MULTIUSER=y
# Network filesystems menu: wraps NFS_FS/NFSD below.
CONFIG_NETWORK_FILESYSTEMS=y
# Network device support menu: wraps CONFIG_VIRTIO_NET below (no "default
# y" at all outside UML, so always needs an explicit enable).
CONFIG_NETDEVICES=y
# "Multiple devices driver" menu: wraps CONFIG_BLK_DEV_DM and every
# CONFIG_DM_* target below (no "default y" at all, always needs an
# explicit enable).
CONFIG_MD=y

# --- boot path: microvm machine, PVH direct boot, virtio-mmio -------------
CONFIG_64BIT=y
CONFIG_SMP=y
CONFIG_PARAVIRT=y
CONFIG_KVM_GUEST=y
CONFIG_HIGH_RES_TIMERS=y
# PVH direct boot: lets qboot start the kernel with no firmware real-mode
# dance at all (test/qemu/scripts/run-qemu.sh, test/qemu/README.md "Fast
# boot").
CONFIG_PVH=y
CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO=builtin
# microvm has no ACPI (run-qemu.sh's acpi=off); the kernel instead learns
# about its virtio-mmio devices from a virtio_mmio.device= kernel command
# line parameter QEMU appends automatically -- this symbol parses it.
CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO_CMDLINE_DEVICES=builtin
# Scratch/source disks every qemu_test with a `disks =` attribute attaches
# (test/qemu/qemu_test.bzl, test/qemu/scripts/run-qemu.sh).
CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK=y
# nfs_test's loopback networking inside the Debian chroot
# (test/qemu/guest/nfs.sh) needs a network stack; kept as virtio-net even
# though nothing today attaches a virtio-net device, matching the existing
# build-kernel.sh baseline this fragment replaces.
CONFIG_VIRTIO_NET=y
CONFIG_VIRTIO_CONSOLE=y
CONFIG_SERIAL_8250=builtin
# run-qemu.sh's `-serial stdio` console=ttyS0.
CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE=builtin
# Kernel boot diagnostics: README.md's boot-time measurement reads a pr_info
# timestamp, and every test's serial.log capture depends on dmesg/boot
# messages for debugging failures.
CONFIG_PRINTK=y
# test/qemu/guest/init execs /bin/busybox (an ELF binary) as the very first
# user process, and every guest/*.sh test script is a #!/bin/sh script.
CONFIG_BINFMT_ELF=builtin
CONFIG_BINFMT_SCRIPT=builtin
# guest/init's initramfs boot.
CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD=builtin
CONFIG_RD_GZIP=builtin

# insmod needs module support at all (no test boots without it any more).
CONFIG_MODULES=builtin

# --- pseudo filesystems every test's guest/init mounts --------------------
CONFIG_DEVTMPFS=builtin
CONFIG_DEVTMPFS_MOUNT=y
CONFIG_PROC_FS=builtin
CONFIG_SYSFS=builtin
# guest/init's /tmp (and every qemu_cc_test's default TEST_TMPDIR when no
# `disks=` is given); TMPFS_XATTR/TMPFS_POSIX_ACL: setattr_test/write_test's
# xattr and ACL-equivalent-to-mode checks, and systemd's own requirement
# (third_party/linux/README.md's systemd section) that tmpfs support both.
CONFIG_TMPFS=builtin
CONFIG_TMPFS_XATTR=y
CONFIG_TMPFS_POSIX_ACL=y
CONFIG_SHMEM=y

# --- backing filesystems under test (step 5.2: ext4, xfs, btrfs) ----------
CONFIG_EXT4_FS=y
CONFIG_EXT4_FS_POSIX_ACL=y
# write_test's security.capability-stripping checks.
CONFIG_EXT4_FS_SECURITY=y
CONFIG_BTRFS_FS=y
CONFIG_BTRFS_FS_POSIX_ACL=y
CONFIG_XFS_FS=y
CONFIG_XFS_POSIX_ACL=y
# ext4 casefold (Phase 16: dcfs rejects case-insensitive directories, so the
# test guest needs a kernel that can create one to test the rejection) and
# fscrypt (Phase 16 likewise rejects encrypted directories).
CONFIG_UNICODE=y
CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION=y
# Phase 18 (EDQUOT): disk quotas on the backing filesystems above.
CONFIG_QUOTA=y
CONFIG_QFMT_V2=y
CONFIG_QUOTACTL=y

# --- compression/crc support the above filesystems select -----------------
# ZLIB_INFLATE/ZLIB_DEFLATE/LZO_COMPRESS/LZO_DECOMPRESS/ZSTD_COMPRESS/
# ZSTD_DECOMPRESS are deliberately NOT listed here even though btrfs needs
# them: they're prompt-less symbols (no prompt string after `tristate` in
# lib/Kconfig), Kconfig only lets `select` turn them on, and
# CONFIG_BTRFS_FS already `select`s all of them -- forcing them directly
# from a fragment has no effect and olddefconfig silently recalculates them
# away, which is exactly what README.md's "Kconfig dependency notes" warns
# about. Likewise CONFIG_SUNRPC (NFS_FS and NFSD both `select` it) and the
# old CONFIG_LIBCRC32C (removed from the kernel some releases back; CRC32C
# support is CONFIG_CRYPTO_CRC32C below now).
CONFIG_CRYPTO_CRC32C=y

# --- FUSE, with passthrough -------------------------------------------
CONFIG_FUSE_FS=y
# passthrough_test, write_test's 64 MiB read/write: dcfs serves file content
# via the kernel's FUSE passthrough path instead of round-tripping every
# byte through the daemon.
CONFIG_FUSE_PASSTHROUGH=y
CONFIG_FUSE_IO_URING=y
CONFIG_IO_URING=y

# --- NFS export and the real NFSv4 round trip (nfs_test) -------------------
CONFIG_FHANDLE=y
CONFIG_EXPORTFS=y
CONFIG_NFSD=y
CONFIG_NFSD_V4=y
# Without this, nfsd upcalls to a userland client-tracking daemon on first
# SETCLIENTID; see test/qemu/README.md's "Findings from getting nfs_test
# green" for the rpc.mountd segfault this avoids entirely.
CONFIG_NFSD_LEGACY_CLIENT_TRACKING=y
CONFIG_NFS_FS=y
CONFIG_NFS_V4=y

# --- networking (NFS/SUNRPC's RPC transport, nfs_test's loopback) ----------
CONFIG_UNIX=y
CONFIG_NET=y
CONFIG_INET=y

# --- loop device, event/notification primitives dcfs and its tests use ----
CONFIG_BLK_DEV_LOOP=y
CONFIG_EVENTFD=y
CONFIG_EPOLL=y
CONFIG_SIGNALFD=y
CONFIG_TIMERFD=y
CONFIG_INOTIFY_USER=y
CONFIG_FILE_LOCKING=y
CONFIG_FUTEX=y
CONFIG_POSIX_MQUEUE=y

# --- device-mapper (Phase 11: dm-log-writes power-loss replay, fsfreeze,
# I/O error injection via dm-flakey/dm-delay; "error" is dm-mod's
# own built-in target, no separate symbol) -------------------------------
CONFIG_BLK_DEV_DM=y
CONFIG_DM_DELAY=y
CONFIG_DM_LOG_WRITES=y
CONFIG_DM_FLAKEY=y

# --- namespaces and the new mount API (Phase 15: mount.dcfs wrapper's
# throwaway-namespace capture; systemd's PrivateNetwork=/PrivateUsers=) ----
CONFIG_NAMESPACES=y
CONFIG_UTS_NS=y
CONFIG_IPC_NS=y
CONFIG_USER_NS=y
CONFIG_PID_NS=y
CONFIG_NET_NS=y

# --- systemd guest (wave 7 fill-in, Phase 15.1's systemd-booting Debian
# guest): kernel options from systemd's own README "REQUIREMENTS" section.
# DEVTMPFS, PROC_FS, SYSFS, FHANDLE, UNIX, NET, NET_NS, USER_NS,
# TMPFS_XATTR/TMPFS_POSIX_ACL, {EXT4,XFS,BTRFS}_*_POSIX_ACL are already
# enabled above for other reasons.
CONFIG_CGROUPS=y
CONFIG_AUTOFS_FS=y
CONFIG_SECCOMP=y
CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER=y

# --- R2 (review M3, L8): EXPERT-gated symbols tinyconfig turns off -------
# `bool ... if EXPERT` symbols default to y in a normal kernel but tinyconfig
# (allnoconfig) turns them off, silently. Each is enabled because something
# in the guests needs it:
# timer_create/setitimer/alarm: GNU `timeout` (nfs.sh's `timeout 10 mount
# -t nfs4` in the Debian chroot), systemd, sleep-based test helpers. Without
# it a hung mount never times out.
CONFIG_POSIX_TIMERS=y
# kcmp(2): systemd (its README lists CONFIG_KCMP), fd comparison in tests.
CONFIG_KCMP=y
# io_submit(2) and friends: xfstests' aio-dio tests and fio (Phase 17),
# libaio users in the Debian chroot.
CONFIG_AIO=y
# System V IPC: shm/sem/msg used by Debian userland, fio, ipcs; a normal
# kernel always has it.
CONFIG_SYSVIPC=y
# madvise(2)/posix_fadvise(2): coreutils' dd/cp/sync and xfstests helpers
# call them (an ENOSYS is usually ignored, which hides the loss).
CONFIG_ADVISE_SYSCALLS=y
# membarrier(2): glibc/libgcc runtime use; cheap.
CONFIG_MEMBARRIER=y
# rseq(2): glibc 2.35+ registers it at thread start.
CONFIG_RSEQ=y
# BUG()/WARN() actually trap: without it an assertion failure in a
# filesystem (XFS asserts, btrfs ASSERTs) is silently skipped.
CONFIG_BUG=y
# XFS quota (Phase 18's EDQUOT tests on xfs; QUOTA/QFMT_V2 are above).
CONFIG_XFS_QUOTA=y
# Considered and left off (nothing needs them today; add here if a later
# phase does, e.g. when enumerating the Phase 17 xfstests subset's needs):
# CROSS_MEMORY_ATTACH (process_vm_readv; MPI only), CHECKPOINT_RESTORE and
# PROC_CHILDREN (CRIU), CACHESTAT_SYSCALL, SYSFS_SYSCALL, SGETMASK_SYSCALL,
# MAGIC_SYSRQ, FANOTIFY/DNOTIFY (a handful of xfstests only), XFS_RT,
# FS_VERITY (dcfs does not serve verity), DM_SNAPSHOT/DM_THIN_PROVISIONING
# (xfstests' dm-thin tests are not in the planned subset), COREDUMP,
# BINFMT_MISC, PRINTK_TIME. xfstests (Phase 17) generic tests on the
# fuse/.dcfs mount need, beyond the above: AIO, QUOTA (present), FALLOCATE
# via the filesystems (present), loop (present), dm-flakey/log-writes
# (present).
